title: Runtime Guardrails and Metric Enforcement Spec
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This specification defines a practical, implementation-oriented approach to runtime guardrails for LLM inference on the Redwood platform. It focuses on:
- Metric definitions to detect safety and quality regressions in production.
- Enforced thresholds and runtime actions (block, throttle, transform, fallback).
- Lightweight evaluation hooks (local and hosted evals) integrated into the serving path.
- Operational playbook for incidents and rollouts.

Goal and scope

Goal: prevent user-facing safety, hallucination, and high-cost regressions by enforcing measurable, auditable runtime policies that are aligned with offline evals.
Scope: hosted API and Dedicated; Private deployments should adapt enforcement to customer policy but can reuse metric definitions and hooks here. Does not include model training safety checks.

Terminology

- Guardrail: a runtime policy that evaluates inference outputs or request metadata and produces an action (allow, modify, block, fallback).
- Enforcement point: where the guardrail runs (pre-inference, post-inference, post-decode).
- Signal: measurable item (toxicity score, hallucination-likelihood, token-cost, latency).
- Hook: a light-weight function call from runtime to compute a signal (e.g., run a fast toxicity classifier).

Core guardrail signals and thresholds

Canonical runtime signals and recommended defaults (teams may adjust with approval):

| signal_id | description | computation location | recommended threshold | severity |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| G1.toxicity_score | fast toxicity classifier probability (ensemble) | post-decode hook | >= 0.65 => review; >= 0.85 => block | high |
| G2.hallucination_indicator | overlap ratio with provided context / factuality model score | post-decode analyzer | hallucination_score >= 0.7 => flag | medium |
| G3.personally_identifiable_info | PI detection (regex + model) | post-decode | any hit on PII whitelist => redact & block if user-provisioned data | high |
| G4.token_cost_est | estimated per-request token cost given generation length | pre-inference estimator | > 50k tokens => throttle/deny | low |
| G5.response_length_anomaly | z-score of length vs baseline per-route | post-decode | z >= 3 => sample for investigation & rate-limit | low |
| G6.latency_ms | 95th percentile latency per-model per-route (rolling 5m) | runtime metric | > 2000ms => route to fallback pool | medium |

Concrete enforcement actions

Each guardrail maps to one or more actions. Actions are implemented in the routing and response layer and must be idempotent and auditable.

- ALLOW: return output unchanged and log signal events.
- REDACT: run deterministic transformation to redact the sensitive segment and return modified content.
- BLOCK: return a standardized 403-style structured error with reason and safe fallback.
- FALLBACK: route to a safer small model with constrained decoding (e.g., instruction-tuned 7B quantized) and append audit metadata.
- THROTTLE: decrement per-customer tokens or apply a short circuit to queued requests.

Mapping examples

- G1.toxicity_score >= 0.85 => BLOCK (policy: block + create incident ticket + audit log).
- G3.personally_identifiable_info => REDACT + FALLBACK if request included user-supplied PII.
- G6.latency_ms > 2000ms => FALLBACK to low-latency pool and tag traceback for sampling.

Implementation architecture

1) Signal hooks: lightweight microservices or in-process modules that return a small JSON {signal_id, score, metadata}. Hooks must execute in <= 50ms p95 for post-decode signals on average inference sizes.

2) Enforcement engine: a stateless decision layer in the proxy that applies policy rules and emits actions. This is pluggable via a policy DSL (see sample below).

3) Audit store: append-only event stream (Kafka topic: audits.guardrails) and short-term datastore for quick queries (ClickHouse/Elastic).

4) Fallback pools: pre-configured model variants (safe-small, constrained-decoder, knowledge-grounded) registered in model-catalog with IDs used by enforcement engine.

Policy DSL (example rule)

Rule syntax (pseudo-YAML) used by enforcement engine:

- id: block_high_toxicity
  when:
    - signal: G1.toxicity_score
      operator: ">="
      value: 0.85
  action: BLOCK
  notify: [team-safety, infra-oncall]
  sample_for_review: 1.0

Operational checklist for integrating a new guardrail

1) Define signal: name, computation method, required latency budget.
2) Implement hook: lightweight inference or deterministic extractor; include unit tests.
3) Offline validation: run the hook across 1M stored inference traces; compute precision/recall for labeled subset.
4) Canary roll: enable evaluation-only mode (no actions) for 48-72 hours and surface aggregated alerts.
5) Gradual enforcement: 0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7-14 days with AB metrics tracked (safety, latency, cost, user engagement).
6) Post-rollout audit: export all BLOCK/REDACT/FALLBACK events and human-review a stratified sample.

Alerting, monitoring and SLOs

- SLOs (examples):
  - Guardrail decision latency: p95 < 120ms for post-decode hooks (measured at proxy).
  - Audit event delivery: 99.9% delivered to audits.guardrails in 30s.
  - False-block rate on labeled sets: <= 0.5% for high-severity blocks after 30-day post-rollout review.

- Alerts:
  - Safety spike: sudden increase in BLOCK events by >200% over 5m => page safety team (pagerduty).
  - Hook errors: >1% error rate in hook execution over 5m => page infra oncall.
  - Cost anomaly: average token_cost_est up > 2x baseline over 10m => page product-owner.

Regression triage integration

When a regression is detected in offline evals the triage steps must include:
1) Check whether the failing eval set maps to an existing runtime signal (G1..Gn).
2) If so, extract audit events for matching requests and surface three representative examples with metadata (model_id, prompt, user_route, signals, timestamp).
3) If not, propose a new signal and prototype a hook using the eval harness in eval-harness/.

Incident playbook excerpt (safety block storm)

1) Immediate action: flip the global enforcement gate to evaluation-only for the suspected rule set.
2) Triage: collect top 100 BLOCK events for human review; determine if thresholds were miscalibrated or model behavior changed.
3) Mitigation: either adjust threshold (temporary) or deploy fallback routing to safe-small for affected routes.
4) Postmortem: 3-day timeline for preliminary findings; include regression delta vs offline eval baselines.

Data retention and auditing

- Audit events retained in ClickHouse for 90 days for fast queries; raw payloads (user content) retained in encrypted GCS for 30 days unless required by legal.
- Redaction policy: when REDACT action occurs, store only redaction metadata in fast store and move raw original to encrypted cold store with restricted access.

Testing and validation guidance

- Unit tests: coverage for hooks and enforcement engine rules.
- Integration tests: simulate end-to-end requests with instrumentation to assert actions and latencies.
- Offline simulation: use the eval-harness to replay a stratified sample of production traffic and assert expected actions at thresholds.
- Synthetic adversary tests: maintain a prompt set that attempts to evade filters (stored in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/adversarial-guardrail-suite).

Rollout and change control

- Any change to an enforcement rule that escalates severity or adds BLOCK behavior must be approved by safety and infra leads and follow canary cadence.
- Major guardrail additions require an RFC and a 30-day evaluation-only period on production traffic before enforcement.

Ownership and contacts

- Guardrail platform owner: eng-safety@redwood.com (team: Platform Safety).
- Enforcement engine maintainer: runtime-routing@redwood.com (team: Serving Runtime).
- Oncall routing: eng-sre oncall (see eng-sre/runbooks for schedules).

Examples and CLI snippets

Query audit events (ClickHouse example):
SELECT timestamp, model_id, route, signal_id, score, action
FROM audits_guardrails
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 100

Enable evaluation-only for a rule via admin CLI:
redwood-admin guardrail update --id block_high_toxicity --eval_only true

Policy export (for review):
redwood-admin guardrail export --output /tmp/guardrail-policy-2025-02.json
